name: Button
description: Actions with a clear hierarchy. Use one primary action per region, secondary for alternatives, and ghost for low emphasis.

good: A single primary “Save changes” in a settings form.
bad: Two primary buttons side by side in the same dialog.
boundary: A destructive action must pair danger hierarchy with explicit confirmation.

guidance.summary: Starts an action on the current page, such as saving, sending, confirming, or opening a dialog. A button does something; a link goes somewhere.
useWhen: A person triggers something that changes data, submits a form, or opens a dialog, drawer, or menu.
One action is the main way forward in a region, with alternatives beside it.
An action deletes or sends something that cannot be taken back, shown as danger and confirmed before it runs.

avoidWhen.text: The action takes the person to another page or address. Use a link, so it can be opened in a new tab and its address copied.
The control is only an icon.
The action reports its progress while it runs, such as Saving… then Saved.
A person switches between views or values rather than starting an action.

states.label: Default
states.description: Ready to press. Primary is filled, secondary is outlined, ghost has no surface until hovered, and danger is red for actions that destroy something.
states.how: variant: primary, secondary, ghost, or danger

states.label: Hover
states.description: The surface shifts and lifts slightly under a pointer. It is never the only sign that the button can be pressed.

states.label: Focus
states.description: A focus ring shows which button the keyboard is on.

states.label: Pressed
states.description: The button sinks slightly while it is held, so the press is felt before anything happens.
states.how: Pointer down, or Enter or Space held.

states.label: Disabled
states.description: Visible but unavailable: it cannot be focused or pressed, so the reason must be shown nearby.

dos.title: One primary per region
dos.description: A single filled button shows the way forward; two compete.

dos.title: Verb-first labels
dos.description: Save changes, Send invite: people know the result before they press.

dos.title: Confirm the irreversible
dos.description: Mark delete, send, and pay as consequential, and confirm them.

dos.title: Primary goes last
dos.description: Cancel first, then the action, in the same order on every screen.

donts.title: Buttons that navigate
donts.description: Going to another page is a link, so it can open in a new tab.

donts.title: Disabled with no reason
donts.description: It can’t be focused, so people never learn what is missing.

donts.title: Vague labels
donts.description: OK, Submit, or Click here don’t say what will happen.

donts.title: Danger for emphasis
donts.description: Red that marks everything stops warning about what is permanent.

content: Sentence case, one to three words, no end punctuation.
Match the label to what the title promised: under Delete project, the button says Delete project, not Confirm.

notes: A native button element, so its role, focus, and keys come from the browser.
A button that only shows an icon needs an accessible name; use Icon button.
A disabled button leaves the tab order, so its reason must be written where people can read it.

variant.description: One primary per region. Danger only for destructive actions.

consequential.description: Set true when pressing it changes something outside the screen, such as Delete. Its requests then report consequential: true.
